### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 40 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e23180f04a1218c1ed8c675a3ead446e65ac35a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc30357652fe0c8ed4a12ea8361d727aeaf11a3a` — the merge of head `a66e100b8c9ddb3ac2fa5b64101e75cccb8f865a` into base `6e23180f04a1218c1ed8c675a3ead446e65ac35a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc30357652fe0c8ed4a12ea8361d727aeaf11a3a && git checkout cc30357652fe0c8ed4a12ea8361d727aeaf11a3a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e23180f04a1218c1ed8c675a3ead446e65ac35a a66e100b8c9ddb3ac2fa5b64101e75cccb8f865a && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e23180f04a1218c1ed8c675a3ead446e65ac35a && git merge --no-ff a66e100b8c9ddb3ac2fa5b64101e75cccb8f865a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e23180f04a1218c1ed8c675a3ead446e65ac35a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e23180f04a1218c1ed8c675a3ead446e65ac35a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review: PASS

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A4 · Fixes #33411 (p3) · head `fe338b465099a3bd6c18c90a098d3555878d58ce` · Clause-② no. CI on this head at review time: 17 success, 16 skipped, 15 in progress, none failing.

**What was checked** (read-only: the diff, the card, and `resolveTenantFieldName` in `core/src/security/tenant-field.ts` on this head):

- **(a) Existing-row match.** `loadExistingRecords` now filters a per-organization replay on `organizationColumnOf(objectName)`, which is `resolveTenantFieldName(definition) ?? 'organization_id'`. That is the predicate the engine and the driver wall by, and the reading `probeScopeOf` (#33409) already scopes a reference target by. An unreadable registry keeps `organization_id`, the pre-PR filter. This is also the safety point the comment names: matching on the walled column keeps an upsert from finding another organization's row.
- **(b) One column for the row's organization.** `seedRowTenantColumn` is now the single answer, and `seedRowNeedsOrganization` delegates to it. It feeds:
  - the stamp;
  - the named refusal (its `field` and message);
  - the stamped-reference skip;
  - `organizationOfRow` for seed files;
  - the per-row write options, at all three write sites, including the new `rowOrganization` argument of `writeRecord`.

  An unresolved definition keeps `organization_id`, as the stamp did.
- **No change for every current object.** `resolveTenantFieldName` returns `organization_id` whenever the object has that field and declares no other existing `tenantField`. So for an object with an authored `organization_id`, the result is the same column the old `hasOwnProperty(fields, 'organization_id')` branch answered. The injected-only case still falls to `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(...).tenant`, and tenancy disabled still answers `null`. The only objects whose answer moves are those whose declared `tenancy.tenantField` exists on the object.
- **The one behaviour change is right.** An object that declares a `tenantField` and also carries `organization_id` is now stamped only on the declared column. The engine and the driver wall such an object by that column (both through `resolveTenantField`), so stamping `organization_id` there was writing a column the wall never reads. A seed row that sets `organization_id` itself still keeps it, because only the walled column is stamped. No object in the repo declares a non-default `tenantField`, so nothing shipped moves.
- **Tests.** The real `AppPlugin` + `SqlDriver` integration case goes from 2 failed out of 21 to 21 passed. The two ablations each red their own case. Ablation B shows the driver's insert hook stamping `workspace_id` anyway, so the visible effect of (b) is the named refusal. That case is pinned.

**Semver:** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. Nothing an author writes is refused or re-read; a platform loader stamps and matches on the column the wall already used. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `patch`.

**Nits (none blocking):**

- **N1:** the `organizationColumnOf` jsdoc sits between the previous method's jsdoc and `loadExistingRecords`. The older block ("…a new write without an organization is stamped or refused (D9).") now documents `organizationColumnOf` rather than the method it was written for. Move the new method above that block, or below `loadExistingRecords`.
- **N2:** #33554 (a global object replayed per organization still throws `INVALID_FILTER`) is correctly out of scope. `organizationColumnOf` answers `organization_id` for a tenancy-disabled object, which is exactly that card's filter, so that card's fix will land in this same helper.

Nits only, so this is the final round. Land once CI is green.
